pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT  | Sev2 | Elevated IPv6 egress failures observed from eu-west-3 to multiple customer endpoints. Paging oncall.
Sasha: oncall here, ack. looking.
Jamal: I'm next on rotation, jumping in with packet captures.
Carmen (netops): I see the same alerts in edge-metrics. egress packet loss spikes around 03:08-03:12 UTC. Traceroute to a few destinations shows the last hop acking but payloads never complete.
Sasha: any correlated deploys or config pushes in eu-west-3 around that window?
Carmen (netops): yes — edge firewall policy push at 03:10 from infra-team, there was a rule to drop "non-reassembled fragments" we rolled for performance hardening.
Jamal: doing a tcpdump on outbound interface now. seeing TCP flows with MSS > 1280 where subsequent fragments are simply not forwarded (IP6 Fragment headers present then disappear).
Jamal: tcpdump snippet:
```
15:03:18.123456 IP6 2001:db8:aa::1 > 2001:db8:bb::2: frag, next-header TCP, id 0x04d2
15:03:18.123789 IP6 2001:db8:aa::1.443 > 2001:db8:bb::2.39218: Flags [P.], seq 3456:7890, ack 1, win 29200
```
Sasha: ok that points to middlebox dropping fragments. If ICMP "fragmentation needed" is also being rate-limited or dropped, clients won't reduce path MTU and we get silent failures for large responses.
Customer Success - Priya: SpinUpHealth reported repeated 502s for large export requests and we preemptively opened a ticket. They prefer IPv6.
Carmen (netops): confirmed: edge devices show a rule match count incrementing on "drop fragments" for those source prefixes. That rule was part of the 03:10 performance change.
Sasha: mitigation options: 1) temporarily allow fragments on the edge so reassembly can proceed, 2) enforce MSS/clamp to 1280 on egress so fragmentation never occurs, 3) fail traffic to IPv4-only path for impacted tenants. Thoughts?
Jamal: MSS-clamp is preferable short-term. For IPv6 minimum MTU is 1280 bytes; if we force max segment so payload stays below that we avoid fragments. But for many flows we don't control client stacks — best to remove the drop rule then clamp.
Carmen (netops): I'll disable the fragment-drop rule in eu-west-3 edge cluster and apply a targeted MSS-clamp on the NAT-proxy for affected prefixes. Doing a canary patch to two nodes now.
pagerduty-bot: action taken: edge-config rollback fragment-drop in eu-west-3-canary nodes. change id: edgecfg-20260315-eu3-rollback-1
Jamal: running curl -6 -v --limit-rate 1m to a SpinUpHealth export endpoint before/after. Before: connection hangs, retransmits. After: completes, status 200.
curl before:
```
* Connected to 2001:db8:bb::2 port 443 (#0)
> GET /export HTTP/1.1
> 
* (no data after handshake)
* 10 retransmissions
```
curl after:
```
* Connected to 2001:db8:bb::2 port 443 (#0)
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{... large payload ...}
```
Sasha: customer impact summary: approx 12 tenants reported degraded large-payload API responses in eu-west-3; small-packet traffic and IPv4 traffic unaffected. Issue is specific to IPv6 flows that rely on fragmentation rather than negotiated smaller segments.
Customer Success - Priya: initial customer comms sent to SpinUpHealth and two others. They want RCA + ETA for permanent fix.
Carmen (netops): canary OK across two nodes; rolling to rest of eu-west-3 edges now. Also applying MSS clamp rule on NAT-proxies for affected prefixes to prevent recurrence while we finish edge firmware fix.
pagerduty-bot: change deployed: edge-config allow-fragments + nat-proxy tcp-mss-clamp=1280 (eu-west-3 rolling).
Jamal: monitoring tcp retransmits and fragment counters. Retransmit rates back to baseline in the last 6 minutes.
Sasha: next steps: 1) permanent fix — update edge IDS/IPS signature to avoid dropping legitimate IPv6 fragments, verify with lab harness; 2) add automated test in infra CI to exercise IPv6 large responses; 3) schedule edge firmware patch in next maintenance window.
Carmen (netops): note — IDS vendor flagged fragments as evasion vector; we need a more nuanced config than blanket drop. I'll escalate with vendor.
Sasha: handing off incident to Omar for postmortem and customer follow-up. Please include config diffs and packet captures.
Jamal: saved captures to s3://redwood-incident-captures/1911112222/ and attached capture ids in ticket. Also recorded exact commands used to revert and apply clamp.
Command snippets:
```
# disable fragment drop (edgectl is our control plane)
edgectl set-policy --cluster eu-west-3 --name frag-drop --state disabled
edgectl reload --cluster eu-west-3
# apply MSS clamp on nat-proxy (example)
natproxyctl set tcp_mss_clamp --cluster eu-west-3 --prefix 2001:db8:aa::/48 --mss 1280
```
Omar: joining the thread, acknowledged. I'll own the postmortem and customer RCA. Will contact vendor about signature.
pagerduty-bot: Incident status -> Mitigated (monitoring). Pager duty incident closed for active paging; follow-up tasks created.
Sasha: thanks all — great quick coordination. I'll draft the timeline and hand over to Omar. :thumbsup:
Customer Success - Priya: customers have been updated that we're monitoring and will send RCA within 48 hours.
Jamal: leaving runbook notes in the oncall handbook about frag handling and adding a check for IPv6 large-response flows.
Omar: will schedule postmortem sync tomorrow 10:00 UTC.
